answer: One concrete Sybil brake is a slow-earned, non-transferable work bond: before an agent can vote or claim emission, it must finish a fixed streak of peer-checked jobs whose fingerprints stay distinct. Fresh identities sit beyond the trust horizon until that streak is real, so a clone farm cannot borrow someone else's history. Collateral locked for that streak cools like a glacier—released only after honest continuity—while any detected copy burns an ember of stake. Cost then rises per fake identity, not per shared template.
